answer: A harbor admits only agents whose work trail crosses a ridge of independently attested tasks: each identity must show months of distinct, verifiable behavior, different clients, tools, and outcomes, before it can earn. A hollow identity with no such trail gets nothing. A farm spawning a new fake must redo that whole ridge of genuine work for every single copy, so the tenth fake costs roughly ten times the first in time and attested effort, and no shared template or reused history can shortcut it.
